In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of TGFB1 in functional regression and luteolysis of corpus luteum of cyclic mares, and also with the involvement of the activin-like kinase 5, 4 and 7 (ALK5, 4, 7) in prostaglandin F2a (PGF2a) mediated luteolytic action.
the role of TFG and its receptors in the regulation of luteal function in the mare.
the involvement of TGF in functional regression and in the structural luteolisis of the corpus luteum of the mare.

TGF and ALKS are important mediators for the PGF2α‐induced functional and structural regression of the equine CL.
TGF is a luteolysin in mares.
TGF is a key player of luteal regression in mares, and that ALK5, and to some extent ALK4 and 7, are important mediators for PGF2alpha‐induced structural and functional luteolysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TGF pathway is a key mediator for the luteolytic action of PGF2a in the mare.
TGF is a key regulator of luteal cell function and viability.

TGF and its receptor ALKS are involved in the functional regression and structural regression in the mare.
